title: How to invest in broad-market ETFs for simple long-term growth
description: The 'Buy Everything' strategy that beats stock picking.
content:
The stock market is a complex adaptive system. Trying to predict which specific company will win over the next 20 years is incredibly difficult (remember Kodak or Blockbuster?). However, predicting that the *entire economy* will grow over time is a much safer bet. Broad-Market ETFs allow you to own the entire stock market—thousands of companies at once—with a single purchase. This strategy, known as 'Indexing', removes the risk of single-company failure while capturing the wealth generated by human innovation.

Key Takeaways

  • Total Market Coverage: A fund like VTI holds ~3,700 US companies. You own Apple and Amazon, but you also own the small upstarts that will replace them.
  • Self-Cleansing: Indices are Darwinian. Failing companies drop out of the index automatically; growing companies are added. You never have to manually 'sell losers'.
  • Fee Minimization: Broad ETFs cost ~0.03% per year. Active funds cost ~0.80%. This gap compounds into hundreds of thousands of dollars.
  • Behavioral Alpha: Because you are diversified, you are less likely to panic when one specific sector (like Tech or Energy) crashes.

Why It Matters (US Context)

The US market (S&P 500 or Total Market) has returned approximately 10% annually over the last century. While past performance doesn't guarantee future results, betting against the US economy has historically been a losing trade.

The Ticker Menu

You only need one or two funds to build a world-class portfolio.

1. Total US Stock Market

Tickers: VTI (Vanguard), ITOT (iShares), SCHB (Schwab).

What you own: ~100% of the investable US equity market. Large, Mid, and Small caps.

Expense Ratio: 0.03%.

2. Total World Stock Market

Tickers: VT (Vanguard), ACWI (iShares).

What you own: The US plus Europe, Asia, and Emerging Markets. ~9,000 companies.

Expense Ratio: 0.07%.

Why: The ultimate diversification. If the US stagnates and India booms, you own India.

3. S&P 500 (Large Cap)

Tickers: VOO, IVV, SPY.

What you own: The 500 largest US companies.

Nuance: Historically performs 99% identical to VTI. It is a fine choice, but technically less diversified than Total Market.

The 'Core' Strategy

  1. Pick Your Vehicle: Open a Roth IRA at Fidelity/Schwab.
  2. Buy VTI: Allocate 80-100% of your equity portion to this single ticker.
  3. Automate: Set a recurring investment. Buy $500 on the 1st of the month.
  4. Ignore: Do not check the price. Do not read financial news. Just keep buying shares. You are a collector of assets, not a trader of prices.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is it boring?

Yes. That is the point. Investing should be boring like watching grass grow. If you want excitement, take $100 to a casino. Do not gamble with your retirement.

Can I beat the market?

Statistically, no. 90% of professional fund managers fail to beat the index over 15 years. If Wall Street pros can't do it, you likely won't either.

What if the US economy collapses?

If the entire US economy goes to zero, your money in the bank is likely worthless too (currency collapse). Stocks are actually a hedge against currency failure because they represent real assets (factories, IP, land).
